body.statement: Theorem 5. Suppose \(s_J/J\to\rho\ge1/2\). Let \((q_J,\eta_J)_{J\ge2}\) be any sequence of invariant procedures satisfying \(\max_{h\in\mathcal H_{J,s_J}}\mathcal R_h(q_J,\eta_J)=R^*(J,s_J)+o(J^{-1})\), and let \(\mu_{q_J}=q_J\circ\{n\mapsto(n_{00}/J,n_{11}/J,n_{\mathrm m}/J)\}^{-1}\). With \(\mathcal P(\Delta_2)\) endowed with the weak topology, every weak accumulation point \(\mu\) of the sequence \((\mu_{q_J})_{J\ge2}\) lies in \(\mathcal F_\rho\). Conversely, for every measure \(\mu\in\mathcal F_\rho\), there exists a sequence of invariant procedures \((q_J,\eta_J)_{J\ge2}\) such that \(\mu_{q_J}\Rightarrow\mu\) and \(\max_{h\in\mathcal H_{J,s_J}}\mathcal R_h(q_J,\eta_J)=R^*(J,s_J)+o(J^{-1})\).
body.justification: This theorem identifies exactly why the leading minimax value cannot by itself determine limits of exact finite optimizers.
body.gap: HarshawSavjeSpielmanZhang2024 gives covariance guarantees for one estimator and SudijonoDobribanTchetgen2026 separates first- and second-order risk in another model; neither characterizes this measure-valued first-order face.
body.consumer: For each high-mismatch sensitivity sequence, the envelope identifies the macroscopic assignment mixtures that need an exact or smaller-order selection criterion.
